record.paper_title: SOME OPEN QUESTIONS ON ARITHMETIC ZARISKI PAIRS
record.context_brief: Arithmetic Zariski pair status of the original Eyral–Oka sextics
record.original_question: Do the two projective Eyral–Oka curves C+ and C−—a Galois-conjugate pair of irreducible plane sextics of torus type with singularities 2E6 + A5 + A2—form an arithmetic Zariski pair; that is, are the pairs (P², C+) and (P², C−) not homeomorphic even though the curves are Galois conjugate and this paper shows that their projective complement fundamental groups are isomorphic?

evidence.quote: The question about them being an arithmetic Zariski pair remains open but, using the techniques in [7], several arithmetic Zariski pairs can be exhibited by adding lines to the original curves. It is right hence to conjecture that they form an arithmetic Zariski pair themselves.

In Corollary 2.10, we have proved that the fundamental groups of the Eyral-Oka curves are isomorphic, and hence this invariant cannot be used to decide if these two curves, which are not rigidly equivalent, form an arithmetic Zariski pair.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2 = \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$. A reduced plane curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ of degree $6$ is called a sextic of torus type if its defining polynomial $F$ can be written as $F = F_2^3 + F_3^2$, where $F_2, F_3 \in \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ are homogeneous of degrees $2$ and $3$ respectively. The singularities of $C$ are recorded by their ADE-types; the configuration $2E_6 + A_5 + A_2$ means $C$ has exactly two singular points of type $E_6$, one of type $A_5$, and one of type $A_2$.

It is known that within the moduli of irreducible projective sextics of torus type with the prescribed singularity configuration $2E_6 + A_5 + A_2$, there are exactly two complex equisingular components, and they are interchanged by the action of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$. Pick smooth representatives $C_+$ and $C_-$ defined over a number field, conjugate to each other by a non-trivial Galois automorphism. A pair of plane curves $(C_+, C_-)$ is called an arithmetic Zariski pair if $C_+$ and $C_-$ are Galois conjugate but the topological pairs $(\mathbb{P}^2, C_+)$ and $(\mathbb{P}^2, C_-)$ are not homeomorphic.

Question. Do $C_+$ and $C_-$ form an arithmetic Zariski pair? Equivalently, is it true that there is no homeomorphism $\mathbb{P}^2 \to \mathbb{P}^2$ sending $C_+$ onto $C_-$, given that $\pi_1(\mathbb{P}^2 \setminus C_+) \cong \pi_1(\mathbb{P}^2 \setminus C_-)$?
artifact.category_tag: Arithmetic Zariski pairs of plane sextics
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up related work showing that the Eyral–Oka curves can be modified (e.g. by adding lines) to produce arithmetic Zariski pairs, and that several standard invariants (including fundamental groups of the projective complements and the N_C-invariant) fail to distinguish C+ and C-. No source explicitly establishing or refuting that (P², C+) and (P², C-) are non-homeomorphic was found, so the status appears to remain open/unknown.

status_evidence.title: On arithmetic Zariski pairs in degree 6
status_evidence.snippet: Eyral-Oka curves are close to being an arithmetic Zariski pair; the N_C-invariant coincides for the Galois-conjugate projective Eyral-Oka curves.
status_evidence.claim: Standard invariants do not distinguish the two Eyral–Oka curves, indicating the homeomorphism question is not settled by these invariants.

status_evidence.title: A survey on Zariski Pairs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing arithmetic Zariski pairs among irreducible sextics of torus type.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys list the Eyral–Oka pair as an outstanding candidate without confirming the arithmetic Zariski pair property.
